{"verdict":"CHANGES_REQUESTED","lens":"safety_bypass","slice":"WP-SCP-024/024B","reviewed_at":"2026-05-09","summary":"Slice 024B (scaffolder + --restore + check-invocation-log-entry.sh + ADOPT-001 §12.8) reviewed under the SAFETY_BYPASS lens. 0 CRIT, 6 MAJ, 4 MIN, 2 nit findings. The cascade-status fail-closed default is correctly implemented and verified: all non-enumerated values exit non-zero, the CI=true bootstrap guard fires unconditionally before argument parsing, and the four worked-example test matrix cases 5–8 all genuinely fail. No shell-injection surface was found in Python heredoc invocations (argv-based path passing, re.escape on slug). MANIFEST.json emits no secrets. The fork-PR if: clause is present in the adopter-wrapper template. The three-gate break-glass procedure is correctly three-step and not collapsible to a one-button kill-switch. The six MAJ findings are: (1) --pr mode parse_entry_repo scans the entire PR patch rather than only the branch-protection-log.md file, so an adversarial +### line in any modified file in the PR can spoof the target-repo extraction used for onboarded and onboarded-operator-bump; (2) re.search first-match on cascade-status enables an onboarded-operator-bump slice to escape the TF-row check if a stray cascade-status: onboarded line appears earlier in the DISPATCH-NOTE; (3) the --restore log block emits enforce_admins: ${ENFORCE_ADMINS} (command-line default 'true') and Required check: ${REQUIRED_CONTEXT} (command-line default) rather than the values actually contained in the pre-state JSON being PUT, making the audit trail contradict the Before/After JSON blocks in the same log entry; (4) --restore mode validates only the JSON shape (repo/branch/before keys present, before is a dict) and accepts any conformant JSON including a crafted object with before:{} that would remove all branch protection from the target repo; (5) ADOPT-001 §12.8 Gate 2 instructs 'pin to last known-good release tag SHA' with 'for example v1.2.0' phrasing that is illustrative rather than prescriptive, with no machine verification that the SHA is a release-tag SHA; (6) Gate 3 (re-enable) has no prerequisite enforcement that Gate 2 was completed, allowing an operator to skip the SHA-pin step and re-arm the gate while the wrapper still points to the defective federation-primitive SHA.","findings":[{"id":"MAJ-BYPASS-001","severity":"MAJ","claim":"In --pr mode, parse_entry_repo receives the ENTIRE PR patch (gh pr diff --patch with no file scope), not just the diff of branch-protection-log.md. Any added line matching '+### <timestamp> — <owner/repo>@<branch>' in any file modified by the PR is parsed as a candidate target repo; the function returns the LAST such match. An adversarial or careless change to any file in the same PR that adds a heading-shaped line can spoof the entry_repo value used in the onboarded and onboarded-operator-bump target-match checks. By contrast, the --diff-base code path correctly scopes to only the log file: 'git diff --unified=0 ${DIFF_BASE}..HEAD -- $BRANCH_PROTECTION_LOG'.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh lines 144-145: branch_log_patch=$(gh pr diff $PR --patch 2>/dev/null || true) — no file-scoping argument. Lines 156-168: parse_entry_repo() processes all lines in the patch and returns the last match for lines starting with '+### '. Lines 147-148 (--diff-base path): branch_log_patch=$(git diff --unified=0 ${DIFF_BASE}..HEAD -- $BRANCH_PROTECTION_LOG) — correctly file-scoped. The em-dash separator (U+2014) required by the regex in parse_entry_repo at line 162 is unusual enough to resist accidental collisions but is trivially injectable by an intentional actor modifying any file in the PR.","impact":"An actor who controls at least one file in the cascade slice PR (e.g. a markdown file, the DISPATCH-NOTE itself, or STATUS.md) can add a line of the form '### 2026-05-09T00:00:00Z — jrnb2024/pim@main' to that file and cause parse_entry_repo to return 'jrnb2024/pim' even if the actual log entry targets a different repo or is absent. In single-operator mode this is self-attack; in future multi-operator / multi-contributor cascade scenarios (when a second maintainer joins, the 2026-07-21 bus-factor-1 review) this becomes a genuine bypass of the target-match assertion. The inconsistency between PR mode (full diff) and diff-base mode (scoped diff) also makes CI behaviour inconsistent depending on how the check is invoked, breaking the 'one spec, two invocation paths' contract.","mitigation":"In the --pr code path, scope the patch fetch to the log file only: replace 'gh pr diff $PR --patch' with 'gh pr diff $PR --patch -- $BRANCH_PROTECTION_LOG' (the -- file-path argument is supported by gh pr diff). This makes the PR and diff-base paths symmetric. Update the test harness to cover a multi-file PR scenario where a non-log file adds a heading-shaped line and confirm entry_repo is extracted only from the log file diff."},{"id":"MAJ-BYPASS-002","severity":"MAJ","claim":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh uses re.search() (first-match) to extract the cascade-status value from the DISPATCH-NOTE. If the DISPATCH-NOTE contains a stray 'cascade-status: onboarded' line before the actual 'cascade-status: onboarded-operator-bump' governance field — a realistic accident via copy-paste from a prior slice's DISPATCH-NOTE — the script evaluates the onboarded check-path instead of onboarded-operator-bump. The onboarded path does NOT check for the TF-024X-renovate-<slug> STATUS.md row, so the entire TF-row enforcement (invariant 2's onboarded-operator-bump third check) is bypassed. The cascade slice can then merge without the required tracked-forward Renovate obligation being recorded in STATUS.md.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh lines 101-112: re.search(r'^\\s*cascade-status:\\s+([a-z-]+)\\s*$', text, re.M) — re.search returns the first match, not the last or the one in the governance section. Lines 175-197: the case statement branches on cascade_status; the onboarded-operator-bump branch at line 182 checks branch_log_modified, entry_repo match, AND STATUS.md TF-row; the onboarded branch at line 177 checks only branch_log_modified and entry_repo match. A DISPATCH-NOTE with 'cascade-status: onboarded' at line 5 (e.g. copied from a prior slice) followed by 'cascade-status: onboarded-operator-bump' at line 40 will extract 'onboarded' from re.search, skip the TF-row check, and exit 0 if the log entry is present and the target matches.","impact":"An operator on the onboarded-operator-bump path (Renovate disabled on adopter; operator-driven bump; Renovate re-enablement tracking required per R-024-07) can have the TF-024X-renovate-<slug> STATUS.md row entirely absent while CI passes. The adopter's Renovate re-enablement obligation is never recorded, breaking the Threshold-A Renovate-cycle tracking. The operator may not notice: CI is green, the slice merges, and the deferred TF is invisible. This directly erodes invariant 2's meaningful-content gate for onboarded-operator-bump.","mitigation":"Replace re.search() with re.findall() and assert exactly one cascade-status line is present (die with an informative error if zero or more than one match is found). Alternatively, require the cascade-status field to appear only in a specifically demarcated header block (e.g. between a known start marker and the first '---' or '##' heading) and scope the regex to that block only. The simplest safe fix is: if re.findall() returns more than one distinct value, die 'FAIL-CLOSED: multiple cascade-status fields found in DISPATCH-NOTE; exactly one is required'; if all values are the same, proceed. Update tests to cover the stray-line scenario."},{"id":"MAJ-BYPASS-003","severity":"MAJ","claim":"The restore_branch_protection() function emits an invocation log block with two fields — '- **enforce_admins:** ${ENFORCE_ADMINS}' and '- **Required check:** `${REQUIRED_CONTEXT}`' — taken from command-line variables (defaults: ENFORCE_ADMINS='true', REQUIRED_CONTEXT='policy-check / scp/policy-check'), NOT from the pre-state JSON being restored. An operator restoring a pre-state that had enforce_admins=false and a custom required-check context will produce a log entry whose header fields contradict the Before/After JSON blocks in the same entry. Any future audit reviewer reading only the header fields will conclude enforce_admins=true and the standard context were restored, when the actual PUT applied the pre-state JSON values.","evidence":"enable-required-check.sh line 118: ENFORCE_ADMINS='true' (default). Lines 177-178: --no-enforce-admins sets ENFORCE_ADMINS='false', but restore-mode compatibility guard at line 186 blocks '--no-enforce-admins' when '--restore' is present, so ENFORCE_ADMINS is always 'true' in restore mode. Lines 362-365 of the log block emitted by restore_branch_protection(): '- **enforce_admins:** ${ENFORCE_ADMINS}' and '- **Required check:** \\`${REQUIRED_CONTEXT}\\`'. Lines 334-337: the actual PUT uses restore_before_json verbatim; the before JSON may contain enforce_admins.enabled=false and a different required_status_checks.contexts array. Lines 369-375: the Before block does show the actual JSON, but the top-level header field 'enforce_admins: true' directly contradicts a before JSON showing 'enforce_admins: {enabled: false}'.","impact":"The audit trail in branch-protection-log.md becomes self-contradictory: the header says enforce_admins: true but the Before JSON shows false. An operator or auditor performing a spot-check at the D-035 invocation-log level (reading only header lines, which is the natural human scan pattern) will reach the wrong conclusion about the restored state. This is a trust-model failure in the audit trail that D-044 explicitly claims is forensically accurate. The REQUIRED_CONTEXT field has the same defect: if the original onboarding used a custom --required-check value, the restore log does not reflect it.","mitigation":"In restore_branch_protection(), extract enforce_admins and the required check context from the restore_before_json Python parse output and pass them as additional variables to the log block, or omit the fields entirely and note that the Before/After JSON blocks are the authoritative record. Simplest fix: add two more print() lines in the Python parse step to output enforce_admins.enabled and required_status_checks.contexts[0] from the before JSON, capture them into shell variables, and use those in the log block header instead of ${ENFORCE_ADMINS} and ${REQUIRED_CONTEXT}."},{"id":"MAJ-BYPASS-004","severity":"MAJ","claim":"The --restore mode of enable-required-check.sh validates only that the supplied JSON has the correct shape (object with non-empty string 'repo', non-empty string 'branch', dict 'before'). It does NOT verify that the 'before' dict is a legitimate GitHub branch-protection payload, that it came from an SCP invocation log entry, or that it contains any required-status-check or enforce_admins fields. A crafted JSON with 'before': {} passes all validation and causes gh api -X PUT to remove all branch protection from the target repo. The ADOPT-001 §12.8 and plan-doc §5.4 prose implies provenance from a prior log entry but this is advisory only.","evidence":"enable-required-check.sh lines 298-321 (Python heredoc): validates state is a dict; validates 'repo', 'branch', 'before' keys present; validates repo and branch are non-empty strings; validates before is a dict. No validation that before contains required_status_checks, enforce_admins, or any GitHub branch-protection field. Line 335-336: printf '%s' \"$restore_before_json\" | gh api -X PUT \"repos/${restore_repo}/branches/${restore_branch}/protection\" --input - — this PUT with an empty or minimal JSON body ({}) will remove all required-status-checks, set enforce_admins=false, and remove required_signatures. ADOPT-001 §12.8 line 1195: 'The pre-state JSON lives at the bottom of every invocation log block... copy it to a local file first before invoking the restore mode' — guidance only, not enforced. D-044 rationale: 'Gate 2's wrapper-SHA-pin is explicit operator consent to step backwards' — but no machine control verifies JSON provenance.","impact":"Any actor with access to the operator's shell session can supply a minimal crafted JSON file (e.g. {\"repo\":\"target/repo\",\"branch\":\"main\",\"before\":{}}) and invoke --restore to remove all branch protection from the target repo. In single-operator mode this requires compromising the operator's session; in an environment where the operator leaves a terminal open or runs scripts from a shared directory, the attack surface is real. The 'before': {} body sent to GitHub's branch-protection PUT endpoint will also succeed (returning 200) because GitHub interprets missing fields as null/disabled. The log block emitted afterward will show the crafted JSON as the 'Before' state, creating a false audit record.","mitigation":"Add a schema-validation step in restore_branch_protection() that verifies the 'before' dict contains at minimum the fields that a GitHub branch-protection GET response would include (e.g. 'required_status_checks' key present, 'enforce_admins' key present). Use a known-safe subset check rather than allowing an empty object. Optionally, add a required field 'scp_invocation_id' that the forward-mode log emission includes (a UUID or timestamp+sha) and that restore mode verifies must be present, making crafted JSONs fail without that field. At minimum, add a warning to the operator prompt (printed before the PUT) showing the parsed restore_before_json and requiring a 5-second pause with a 'does this look like a genuine SCP invocation log before-state?' prompt, analogous to the --no-enforce-admins pause."},{"id":"MAJ-BYPASS-005","severity":"MAJ","claim":"ADOPT-001 §12.8 Gate 2 instructs the operator to 'pin the adopter wrapper SHA in policy-check-wrapper.yml to the last known-good release tag SHA, for example v1.2.0 at 5d4341b...' — the phrasing 'for example' makes this guidance illustrative rather than prescriptive. There is no verification step in the Gate 2 procedure that confirms the SHA being pinned corresponds to a release tag rather than an arbitrary commit on main. An operator performing break-glass under time pressure could pin to the current main HEAD (which might itself be the defective SHA or a commit between releases) and satisfy the letter of Gate 2 while the actual protection is absent. D-044's rationale says 'Gate 2's wrapper-SHA-pin is explicit operator consent to step backwards from current SCP main' but 'stepping backwards from main' does not require a release-tag SHA.","evidence":"ADOPT-001 §12.8 lines 1197-1198: 'pin the adopter wrapper SHA in policy-check-wrapper.yml to the last known-good release tag SHA, for example v1.2.0 at 5d4341b... This is a sibling PR on the adopter repo and should be merged through the adopter's normal review path.' The words 'for example' and 'should' are guidance, not mandated. No verification command is given (unlike §12.7.3 which provides explicit gh api verification commands). D-044 DECISIONS.md row: 'Gate 2's wrapper-SHA-pin is explicit operator consent to step backwards from current SCP main' — the trust model claims explicit consent but does not specify release-tag constraint as a hard requirement.","impact":"If an operator pins to main HEAD (which contains the defect) or to an arbitrary inter-release commit, Gate 2 provides no protection: the wrapper is still pointing at untested or defective SCP code. Gate 3's Renovate bump will then promote that arbitrary SHA to the 'fixed' state rather than a verified release tag. The three-gate structure's safety property depends on Gate 2 being a verified known-good release tag; without that constraint, Gate 2 degrades to a documentation step with no substantive protection.","mitigation":"Amend §12.8 Gate 2 to: (a) replace 'for example v1.2.0 at 5d4341b...' with a concrete verification step: 'Run: gh api repos/jrnb2024/standards-control-plane-/git/ref/tags/v1.2.0 --jq .object.sha to obtain the release-tag SHA; use this exact SHA as the pin, not a main-branch commit SHA'; (b) add an explicit warning: 'MUST be a release-tag SHA — do not use the current main HEAD SHA or any untagged commit'; (c) reference ADOPT-001 §12.7.2 (Renovate preset) and §12.7.3 (verify the gate is live) as the post-Gate-3 confirmation step. Update D-044's rationale to state that Gate 2's protection is contingent on pinning to a release-tag SHA."},{"id":"MAJ-BYPASS-006","severity":"MAJ","claim":"ADOPT-001 §12.8 Gate 3 (re-enable) has no prerequisite check that Gate 2 (SHA pin to known-good release tag) was completed. The procedure describes three sequential gates but nothing in the procedure or the tooling prevents an operator from executing Gate 1 (disable via --restore), then immediately executing Gate 3 (re-enable via enable-required-check.sh) without performing Gate 2. If Gate 2 is skipped, the required check is re-armed while the adopter wrapper still pins the defective federation-primitive SHA, meaning every subsequent PR on the adopter repo hits the defective SCP gate.","evidence":"ADOPT-001 §12.8 lines 1195-1202: Gate 1, Gate 2, Gate 3 described as sequential steps with no gating language between them ('once the SCP federation primitive ships a fixed release tag... re-run scripts/enable-required-check.sh'). enable-required-check.sh has no flag or check that verifies whether the wrapper SHA in the adopter repo has been updated. The plan-doc invariant 7 SLO says '<30 minutes from operator decision to restored state' — a time-pressured operator may skip Gate 2 to meet the SLO. D-044 rationale: 'Gate 3 ensures the adopter does not remain permanently un-gated after the defect is fixed' — correct, but it does not note that Gate 3 must be preceded by Gate 2.","impact":"An operator who skips Gate 2 and executes Gate 3 directly after Gate 1 re-arms the required check against the defective federation-primitive SHA. Every PR on the adopter repo then hits the defect. The intended safety: the defect window is contained until a fixed release is available and Renovate propagates it. The actual outcome when Gate 2 is skipped: the defect window is restored immediately. The break-glass procedure's primary safety property — that Gate 2 provides the 'safe harbor' SHA — is defeated.","mitigation":"Add an explicit numbered prerequisite check at the start of Gate 3 in §12.8: 'Before re-enabling, verify the adopter wrapper SHA has been updated to the fixed release tag SHA: run gh api repos/<adopter>/contents/.github/workflows/policy-check-wrapper.yml | jq -r .content | base64 -d | grep uses: and confirm the SHA is the fixed release tag, not the defective SHA from before Gate 1.' Alternatively, add a --verify-wrapper-sha <expected-sha> flag to enable-required-check.sh that refuses to re-enable unless the adopter repo's wrapper file contains the specified SHA. Update D-044 rationale to state that Gate 3 is only safe AFTER Gate 2 completes."},{"id":"MIN-BYPASS-001","severity":"MIN","claim":"scaffold-downstream.sh accepts any writable directory as --output-dir without a guard against system paths. The validation at lines 127-129 checks only that the directory exists and is writable. Passing --output-dir /etc (if writable) causes mkdir -p /etc/.github/workflows/ and writes four files under that path. The script does not warn on or reject paths outside a user home directory or the expected local-repo checkout tree.","evidence":"scaffold-downstream.sh lines 127-129: 'if [ ! -d \"$OUTPUT_DIR\" ] || [ ! -w \"$OUTPUT_DIR\" ]; then die \"--output-dir must exist and be writable\"; fi'. Lines 143-144: 'WORKFLOWS_DIR=${OUTPUT_DIR}/.github/workflows; mkdir -p \"$WORKFLOWS_DIR\"'. No check that $OUTPUT_DIR resolves within $HOME, the SCP repo root, or any other expected boundary. The CI=true guard (lines 48-50) prevents automated exploitation but bootstrap-only operation still exposes this surface when the operator's PATH or invocation environment is misconfigured.","impact":"Minor in practice (bootstrap-only, operator-run). However, a misconfigured invocation or a wrapping script that passes a computed path could write the adopter wrapper YAML to an unexpected system location. On macOS with standard permissions /etc is not writable, but /tmp and /var are, and a symlink under a user-writable directory could redirect to a sensitive path. The MANIFEST.json written to the path would record the fact but only if the operator reviews it.","mitigation":"Add a home-directory or explicit ancestor check: resolve $OUTPUT_DIR to its canonical path (using readlink -f or Python pathlib.Path.resolve()) and verify it starts with $HOME or the directory of the operator-provided local clone (e.g. validate it is a git work-tree root or a subdirectory thereof). Emit a loud warning (not a hard fail, to allow intentional override) if the resolved path is not under $HOME. Document the intended usage: '--output-dir should be the root of the local clone of the adopter repo'."},{"id":"MIN-BYPASS-002","severity":"MIN","claim":"The --i-understand-this-repo-has-no-prior-green-ci flag is silently accepted and silently ignored when combined with --restore. The restore-mode incompatibility check at enable-required-check.sh:186-190 does not include ACK_NO_PRIOR_GREEN_CI in its list of forward-mode flags, so '--restore file.json --i-understand-this-repo-has-no-prior-green-ci' passes the guard without error. The flag has no effect in restore mode (the green-CI check is guarded by [ -z \"$RESTORE_STATE\" ]) but an operator who includes it may believe it is modifying restore-mode behaviour.","evidence":"enable-required-check.sh line 120: ACK_NO_PRIOR_GREEN_CI=0 (default). Line 181: --i-understand-this-repo-has-no-prior-green-ci sets ACK_NO_PRIOR_GREEN_CI=1. Lines 186-190: restore incompatibility guard checks REPO, BRANCH, PLAN_ONLY, ACK_ADMIN_BYPASS, ENFORCE_ADMINS — ACK_NO_PRIOR_GREEN_CI is not listed. Lines 247-257: green-CI check wrapped in 'if [ -z \"$RESTORE_STATE\" ]' — correctly not executed in restore mode. The flag is therefore parsed, set to 1, and silently ignored. The parallel issue also exists for --enforce-admins (which sets ENFORCE_ADMINS='true', same as default): '--restore file.json --enforce-admins' passes the guard with no warning.","impact":"Operator confusion only — no security bypass. An operator preparing a restore invocation from shell history who copies a prior forward-mode command including the flag will not see an error and may assume the flag had an effect. Low severity but violates the principle of explicit error on nonsensical flag combinations.","mitigation":"Add ACK_NO_PRIOR_GREEN_CI to the restore-mode incompatibility check. Also add --enforce-admins to the check (it sets ENFORCE_ADMINS='true' which equals the default and thus currently passes the ENFORCE_ADMINS != 'true' test). The check should explicitly enumerate all flags that are meaningless in restore mode and reject them with an actionable error message."},{"id":"MIN-BYPASS-003","severity":"MIN","claim":"The cascade-status parser regex r'^\\s*cascade-status:\\s+([a-z-]+)\\s*$' allows leading whitespace (\\s*) before 'cascade-status:'. This means indented lines inside markdown fenced code blocks, YAML literals, or indented prose sections also match. Combined with re.search first-match (MAJ-BYPASS-002), this widens the surface of accidentally matchable lines: a code block demonstrating the cascade-status field (e.g. a DISPATCH-NOTE template section with '    cascade-status: onboarded' indented 4 spaces) would be extracted as the first match even if the actual governance field appears later.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh lines 107-108: re.search(r'^\\s*cascade-status:\\s+([a-z-]+)\\s*$', text, re.M). The \\s* prefix allows 0 or more whitespace characters, matching indented lines. A markdown fenced code block containing '    cascade-status: onboarded' (4-space indent) would match. The DISPATCH-NOTE template (CASCADE-PR-BODY.md emitted by the scaffolder) does not contain cascade-status lines, but prior slice DISPATCH-NOTEs (which authors often use as copy templates) do, and code-block examples in documentation may in future.","impact":"Extends the MAJ-BYPASS-002 first-match surface to include indented content, making accidental or copy-paste-induced stray matches more likely. A DISPATCH-NOTE author who includes an example block showing a prior cascade-status value will have their slice evaluated under the wrong check-path without any diagnostic error.","mitigation":"Remove the leading \\s* and require the field to start at column zero: change to r'^cascade-status:\\s+([a-z-]+)\\s*$'. If indentation support is genuinely needed for some DISPATCH-NOTE format, use re.findall instead of re.search and assert exactly one match (see MAJ-BYPASS-002 mitigation). Update the regex in the test harness to confirm that indented cascade-status lines do not match."},{"id":"MIN-BYPASS-004","severity":"MIN","claim":"The restore_branch_protection() function extracts restore_repo and restore_branch from the pre-state JSON file without the path-traversal guard present in forward mode. Forward mode at lines 234-245 of enable-required-check.sh applies a case-pattern guard (*..*|.*|*/.*|*/..*) and a regex check on REPO and BRANCH before using them in API calls. Restore mode applies only Python isinstance/non-empty-string validation and uses the values directly in 'gh api -X PUT repos/${restore_repo}/branches/${restore_branch}/protection'. A JSON with 'repo': 'jrnb2024/pim\\n' (newline) or 'branch': '../main' passes the Python check and is interpolated into the gh command.","evidence":"enable-required-check.sh lines 308-314 (Python): validates repo is non-empty string and branch is non-empty string — no character-class or pattern check. Line 335: gh api -X PUT \"repos/${restore_repo}/branches/${restore_branch}/protection\" — shell interpolation of JSON-extracted values without traversal guard. Lines 234-245 (forward mode): case '$REPO' in *..*|.*|*/.*|*/..* ) — traversal guard; then grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$'. This guard exists for REPO and BRANCH but has no analogue in restore mode.","impact":"A crafted JSON with a repo containing a newline or path component would cause gh to construct a malformed URL. In practice, gh CLI URL-encodes special characters and GitHub API rejects malformed repo paths with HTTP 404 or 422. The practical impact is a failed restore operation with a non-obvious error message, not a successful exploitation. Severity is MIN because the exploitation path ends in API rejection, not in unintended state mutation.","mitigation":"Apply the same forward-mode guards to restore_repo and restore_branch after they are extracted from the Python parse: add a case-pattern check for path-traversal sequences and a grep -qE pattern check for the owner/name shape. Mirror lines 234-245 logic inside restore_branch_protection()."},{"id":"nit-BYPASS-001","severity":"nit","claim":"test_scaffold_downstream.sh tests the CI=true bootstrap guard (run_expect_exit 1 with CI=true at lines 124-132) but does NOT test the GITHUB_ACTIONS=true guard. scaffold-downstream.sh line 48 has 'if [ \"${CI:-}\" = \"true\" ] || [ \"${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}\" = \"true\" ]' — both env vars must exit 1 per the bootstrap-only contract, but only CI=true is test-covered.","evidence":"test_scaffold_downstream.sh lines 124-132: single test case with env CI=true. No test case for GITHUB_ACTIONS=true. scaffold-downstream.sh line 48-50: both CI and GITHUB_ACTIONS are guarded. The symmetry is present in enable-required-check.sh line 63 (also guards both) but the test coverage in scaffold-downstream.sh only covers one branch.","impact":"If a future refactor of scaffold-downstream.sh mistakenly drops the GITHUB_ACTIONS check while keeping the CI check, the test suite would not catch it. Low risk given the simplicity of the guard, but the 024A R7 CRIT lesson (always test worked examples) applies here: the symmetry claim in D-044 ('refuses CI=true / GITHUB_ACTIONS=true per D-035 symmetry') is only half-tested.","mitigation":"Add a second run_expect_exit 1 test case to test_scaffold_downstream.sh that passes GITHUB_ACTIONS=true (and unsets CI) and expects exit 1. Mirror the existing CI=true test exactly with GITHUB_ACTIONS in the env -i invocation."},{"id":"nit-BYPASS-002","severity":"nit","claim":"D-044 (docs/DECISIONS.md row) describes the cascade-status regex as 'matches in STATUS.md or DISPATCH-NOTE' — a 'file-agnostic' claim. The onboarded-operator-bump implementation in check-invocation-log-entry.sh uses the pattern '^- \\*\\*TF-024X-renovate-{slug}(?:\\*\\*)? \\((open|...)\\): \\S.{19,}$' with '^- \\*\\*' prefix and '$' end anchor, which requires the STATUS.md bullet-list format and will NOT match a TF reference embedded in DISPATCH-NOTE prose. The blocked-on-adopter-conflict pattern correctly omits the prefix/anchor. The D-044 trust-model description's 'file-agnostic' claim is accurate only for the conflict path, not the operator-bump path.","evidence":"docs/DECISIONS.md D-044 row (line 90): 'Regex (Python re): TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+...: \\S.{19,} — matches in STATUS.md or DISPATCH-NOTE.' check-invocation-log-entry.sh lines 192-196 (onboarded-operator-bump): pattern = rf'(?m)^- \\*\\*TF-024X-renovate-{re.escape(slug)}(?:\\*\\*)? \\((open|...)\\): \\S.{{19,}}$' — has '^- \\*\\*' prefix.
